title: Delhi’s air crisis stretches beyond its borders
summary: In Loni, across the border from Delhi, residents describe living beside furnaces and dust-filled roads. Field reports and pollution records trace the haze to several different sources.
body: In Loni, Sneha Mordani’s reporting for NDTV follows residents living with industrial smoke and road dust. Weeks earlier, inspectors had visited 21 furnace sites in the area and recorded violations at each one. Their findings describe those sites. Measuring the contribution of industry across the city takes a different kind of evidence.

The answer changes with the hours and the geography. The Centre for Science and Environment found that traffic accounted for an estimated 52% of pollution attributed to sources inside Delhi from 1 to 8 November. For eight hours after Diwali, a separate IITM estimate reported by The Indian Express attributed 71.1% of Delhi’s fine particles to fireworks.

Farther north, satellites record fires in the paddy belt. The Indian Agricultural Research Institute counted 156 detections in Punjab on 19 November. Estimating how much smoke reached Loni requires wind and atmospheric data as well.
caption: Satellite view of haze across the Indo-Gangetic Plain, 3 November 2024.
credit: Michala Garrison / NASA Earth Observatory, Suomi NPP VIIRS

title: After eight years, BepiColombo reaches Mercury
summary: A shortened engine burn put the spacecraft into safe mode. Flight controllers confirmed it had reached a stable orbit around the planet.
body: BepiColombo launched in October 2018. Over the next eight years it passed Earth once, Venus twice and Mercury six times, using their gravity to shape its approach to the Sun’s innermost planet.

On 21 November 2026, the spacecraft performed its orbit-insertion burn. ESA says a software issue ended the manoeuvre early. When contact resumed, flight controllers found the spacecraft in safe mode and confirmed it was orbiting Mercury.
ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mio are travelling together. The mission calls for them to separate and study the planet and its magnetic environment from different orbits.
caption: Mercury pictured by the earlier MESSENGER mission.
credit: NASA / Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory / Carnegie Institution of Washington

title: What the Rohingya judgment means for survivors
summary: Seven years after The Gambia filed its case, the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the 2017 operations in northern Rakhine State.
body: At the Peace Palace in The Hague, judges issued their ruling on Myanmar’s responsibility under the Genocide Convention. The case dates to November 2019, when The Gambia filed its application. In July 2022 the court dismissed Myanmar’s preliminary objections, allowing the case to proceed.

In Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, Reuters interviewed Rahama Khatun as she followed the ruling. Her account puts a family’s experience beside a judgment that addresses the responsibility of a state. For survivors, the practical question now is how the decision will be carried out.

title: A patchwork recovery on the Great Barrier Reef
summary: After a season of steep losses, divers found hard coral growing back in parts of the reef. A regional average conceals how differently nearby reefs can fare.
body: The Australian Institute of Marine Science surveys hard coral cover across the northern, central and southern Great Barrier Reef. Its 2024–25 survey recorded losses across all three regions following widespread bleaching and other disturbances.

The next field season brought a mixed picture. The institute recorded an increase on 28% of surveyed reefs, a decline on 16% and no net change on the remaining 56%. Scientists and trained tourism crews collect observations at different scales, giving researchers more than one way to follow those changes.

title: Who gained from Manhattan’s congestion toll?
summary: The first year brought fewer vehicles into the charging zone. Delivery operators and shopkeepers describe where the cost of a trip ended up.
body: On the toll’s first anniversary, New York State reported 27 million fewer vehicle entries to the congestion relief zone, an 11% drop. A separate working paper used road-speed observations to estimate how travel times changed across the wider road network.

The effects look different on a delivery invoice. Merchants interviewed during the first week described new surcharges, and a trucking operator later described passing a share of his toll costs on to customers. The MTA’s discount rules show which frequent low-income drivers can receive relief.
caption: Lower Manhattan and its waterways, photographed from space in 2002.
credit: Landsat 7 / USGS EROS via NASA Earth Observatory

title: The part of Chandrayaan-3 that came home
summary: Vikram and Pragyan worked on the Moon. Engineers used fuel left in the propulsion module to send it back into orbit around Earth.
body: Chandrayaan-3 entered lunar orbit on 5 August 2023. Twelve days later Vikram separated from the propulsion module. The lander touched down on 23 August and deployed the Pragyan rover on the surface.

The propulsion module had already delivered the lander. On 4 December, ISRO described how its engineers used the remaining propellant to transfer that module into Earth orbit. The mission log and landing broadcast follow the other two vehicles.

title: The records behind the electoral bonds ruling
summary: The Supreme Court turned down SBI’s request for more time. The hearing hinged on how the bank kept its purchase and redemption records.
body: In February 2024 the Supreme Court struck down India’s electoral bonds scheme and directed the State Bank of India to disclose information about purchases and redemptions. SBI subsequently asked for an extension until June.

The bank said matching the two sets of transactions would take time. On 11 March the court said its order required disclosure of the available records. It ordered SBI to supply them by 12 March. The two judgments show how the dispute moved from voters’ access to information to the practical question of what the bank held.
caption: First page of the Supreme Court’s March 2024 order.
